title: Completion field to support multiple completion multi-fields

timeline.message:
Completion field to support multiple completion multi-fields

The completion field supports multi-fields. In case the sub-field is another completion field, the whole object structure from the incoming document needs to provided as input to the sub-field while parsing it. We have a special XContentParser for this scenario, but it does not handle returning the same object structure multiple times. That is why you can have only one completion sub-field within a completion field, and the error returned when this breaks is a general parsing error that makes users think they have done something wrong in their document.

This commit expands testing for this scenario and extends the parser to support it.

Closes #83534
timeline.author: Luca Cavanna

timeline.body:
The completion field supports multi-fields. In case the sub-field is another completion field, the whole object structure from the incoming document needs to provided as input to the sub-field while parsing it. We have a special XContentParser for this scenario, but it does not handle returning the same object structure multiple times. That is why you can have only one completion sub-field within a completion field, and the error returned when such mechanism breaks is a general parsing error (that mentions a field called dummy_field) that makes users think they have done something wrong in their document.

This commit expands testing for this scenario and extends the parser to support it.

As part of this change, a new parser is created for each sub-field, which makes it possible to expose the same object structure multiple times, for instance in case a completion field has more than one completion sub-fields.

Additionally, the wrapping of both the geo_point multi field parser and the completion multi field parser into a dummy_field object is removed in favour of returning the correct `currentName` of the main field we are parsing.

Additionally getTokenLocation is tweaked to return the location of the field we are parsing in the document, so that error messages become clearer when things go wrong.

Closes #83534

-    private static class CompletionParser extends FilterXContentParser {
+    /**
+     * Parser that exposes the expected format depending on the type of multi-field that is consuming content.
+     * Completion fields can hold multi-fields, which can either parse simple values or an object in case of another completion field.
+     * This parser tries to detect which of the two is parsing content and exposes the full object when needed (including input, context
+     * and weight if available), otherwise the values only.
+     *
+     * A few assumptions are made that make this work:
+     * 1) only string values are supported for a completion field, hence only sub-fields that parse strings are supported
+     * 2) sub-fields that parse simple values only ever call {@link #textOrNull()} to do so. They may call {@link #currentToken()} only to
+     * check if there's a null value, which is irrelevant in the multi-fields scenario as null values are ignored in the parent field.
+     * 3) completion is the only sub-field type that may be parsing the object structure.
+     *
+     * The parser is set to expose by default simple values, unless {@link #nextToken()} is called which is what signals that the
+     * consumer supports the object structure. Note that in order to support multiple completion sub-fields, the inner object parser
+     * needs to be able to return the same object structure multiple times.
+     */
+    /*
+    There are a couple of problems with the current approach: the parser changes behaviour depending on which methods are called by
+    consumers, which is extremely delicate. This kind of works for our internal mappers, but what about mappers from plugins?
+    Also, the sequence of tokens returned by this parser is not valid and things like e.g. copyCurrentStructure blow up.
+    Additionally {@link #getTokenLocation} is incorrect, which is reported together with error messages.
+     */

reply.body: Passing a Map was what we did before and it caused problems of its own.  I like the idea of creating a new parser for each multifield though, that feels a lot cleaner.
It should be possible to create a new parser for each multi-field, I am working on a follow-up that should allow to remove some of this complexity. Do you mind if we merge this one in the meantime?

with the recent changes, two out of three problems that I listed are solved. The fact that the parser is delicate stays, as it changes behaviour depending on what consumers do, but I think I can accept that given that it's the only one that does this.

timeline.body:
I have removed the wrapping, I am not sure why it was needed. We do have the problem now that currentName at the top-level is null hence if something breaks during parsing, users get an error with a null field name, whereas they would get an error about dummy_field before. I don't see other places where the top-level field could be used.

On the other hand, if there are errors while parsing the document they happen mostly when parsing the parent field, and multi-field parsing should go smooth unless we have bugs.
